subject: Urgent: Vanguard p95 surge — emergency patch activation / rollback consent
messages:
From: Aimee Chen <aimee.chen@vanguard.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, infrastructure@vanguard.com
Cc: Paul Ng <paul.ng@vanguard.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Dec 2026 08:12:00 -0500
Subject: Urgent: P95 latency spike after v5.2 deploy

Team —

We just saw a sudden jump in inference p95 across our production traffic starting ~07:45 ET after your v5.2 rollout. Baseline p95 was ~180ms; current p95 is ~650ms and some customer flows are timing out. Error rate is still low but user-facing latency is breaking our SLA (p95 target 300ms). I attached a quick summary with timestamps and sample traces.

This is blocking key repro flows for our quoting microservice. We need an immediate mitigation: either a targeted variant fallback or a full rollback to v5.1 while you investigate. Our procurement/ops team is standing by — we can accept a brief maintenance window if you lead the rollback.

We are sensitive to rollback side effects, so please call out potential cache-warmup and KV impacts in your plan.

Aimee
Senior Platform Engineer
Vanguard Financial Services

Attachment: vanguard_latency_summary_20261209.pdf
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Dec 2026 09:05:00 -05:00
Subject: RE: Urgent: P95 latency spike after v5.2 deploy

Naomi / Ben / Hannah —

Thanks Aimee. Triage summary from SRE (initial): the v5.2 kernel path increases KV cache thrash when request mix includes long prefixes; this only surfaces at >60% tail concurrency, which Vanguard's traffic pattern hit during a batch job. We have a rollback playbook ready (attached).

Proposed immediate action:
- 13:30 ET: schedule 10-minute maintenance window (inform customers)
- 13:32 ET: execute controlled rollback from v5.2 -> v5.1 using canary-unpin (traffic split 0->100 over 3 minutes)
- 13:40 ET: monitor p95 for 30 minutes; if stable, finalize rollback and start post-mortem

Questions for sign-off:
- Ben: do we approve a temporary SLA carveout and a customer-facing credit (if needed) or do we need legal to sign an amendment first?
- Naomi: any compliance or contract constraints on a forced rollback for Vanguard?
- Hannah: can SRE commit to the 13:32 ET execution and confirm rollback runbook steps below are safe?

I’ve attached rollback_playbook_v5.2.md (runbook + rollback verification queries). If we get approval, I will send the maintenance notice to Aimee and coordinate the execution channel.

—Marcus
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment: rollback_playbook_v5.2.md
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Dec 2026 11:18:00 -05:00
Subject: RE: Urgent: P95 latency spike after v5.2 deploy

Marcus —

SRE standing by and confirmed runbook. Quick notes:
- Execution will cause brief cache-warmup; expect a temporary p50 improvement then stabilization over ~7 minutes.
- There is a small chance of increased tokenization latency on some shards during the first 2 minutes as KV caches rehydrate. We will throttle background warmup to prevent overload.
- We will run rollback on the dedicated pool for Vanguard only to limit blast radius.

Can commit to the 13:32 ET execution time. I attached the checklist we will use for the run (sre_execution_checklist.txt).

Hannah
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachment: sre_execution_checklist.txt
